subject.title: refactor: move provider transports into packages/ai behind a typed host port

question: Should `@openclaw/ai/transports` become a supported extension-facing API, or should this refactor retain package-private transport implementations behind existing SDK facades?
rationale: The branch explicitly exports, documents, and maps this new subpath for extension resolution, creating a compatibility contract that cannot be safely inferred from an internal refactor alone.

options.title: Keep transports private
options.body: Restrict the new package entrypoint to internal/package-private use and retain only narrow existing facades for supported plugin integration.

options.title: Adopt a supported transport API
options.body: Keep the public subpath but reduce it to an intentional documented contract with compatibility tests and named long-term ownership.

recommendation.title: Keep transports private
recommendation.body: Restrict the new package entrypoint to internal/package-private use and retain only narrow existing facades for supported plugin integration.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the proposed host-port and export design, so is best positioned to clarify the intended package boundary.
